paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the first bar, the lighter bar is 39.50%, and the darker bar is only 0.04%). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning on certain key principles eliminates bias to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across prompts specific to Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, also considerably reducing bias across Virtual Contact prompts.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the bias percentages before and after instruction tuning for three categories: Support of Authorities, Extended Contact, and Virtual Contact. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled and ordered from left to right, with each category having a linear scale. The vertical axis represents the bias percentage, labeled and scaled from 0 to 70 in increments of 10. The chart displays grouped bars for each category, with colors representing different contact types: No Contact Before (light gray), Positive Contact Before (pink), Negative Contact Before (blue), No Contact After (dark gray with diagonal lines), Positive Contact After (red with diagonal lines), and Negative Contact After (dark blue). In the Support of Authorities category, the light gray bar is approximately 39.50, the pink bar is around 31.83, and the blue bar is about 42.38, with corresponding dark gray, red, and dark blue bars significantly shorter, at 0.04, 0.00, and 0.00, respectively. The Extended Contact category shows a light gray bar at 40.61, a pink bar at 36.13, and a blue bar at 47.28, with a dark blue bar at 0.11 and no visible dark gray or red bars. The Virtual Contact category has light gray, pink, and blue bars at 39.74, 39.17, and 43.83, respectively, with corresponding dark gray, red, and dark blue bars at 10.00, 10.01, and 10.02. The bars are not sorted in any specific order within their categories, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding.
